metaDescription: Six Kenmore canister vacuums explained by series, from the 200 and 400 sealed HEPA models to the 500 bagless, the 600 Pet PowerMate and the Elite Ultra Plush.
expertTake: The Kenmore 600 Series with the Hair Eliminator brushroll is the best all-round pick because it adds a self-clearing brush and a stair grip to the two-motor body. The Kenmore 81214 is the value pick for sealed HEPA at the entry tier. Anyone with thick plush carpet should look at the Elite Ultra Plush 700, and anyone wanting a quiet premium machine should look beyond the range.
introParagraphs: This brand sells canister vacuums in a ladder of numbered series, and the numbers are the easiest way to understand what you are buying. Each step up adds something specific: a sealed air path, a self-clearing brush, a bagless cyclone, a powered pet nozzle or a head tuned for plush carpet. Everything shares the same basic body, so the choice is about which extra you need.

Because the series overlap, listings can be confusing, and the same machine often appears under several names. The sections below decode the ladder by what each rung adds, and rank the six machines that best represent it. Where a feature is not stated in a listing, the guide says so rather than guess.

products.name: Kenmore 600 Series bagged canister with Hair Eliminator brushroll, stair grip
products.description:
The top of the current mid-range series is the best all-rounder because it combines every convenience feature in one machine. A Hair Eliminator brushroll clears itself of hair, a Pet PowerMate attachment lifts embedded fur from carpet, and the Pop-N-Go tool switches between carpet and bare floor without bending.

A telescoping wand extends to 9.5 ft for floor-to-ceiling work, a detachable handle helps above the floor and a stair grip gives a secure hold when carrying the body. Two motors keep suction strong while the brush spins. Compared with the 81615 in the same series it adds the self-clearing brushroll and the grip.

The cost is weight, since a two-motor body is not light, and a bag you must change before it fills. Check the roller ends for stray hair and replace filters on schedule. For a carpeted home with pets and stairs it is the one to buy. Because the stair grip is a handle moulded into the body, it is also the easiest to lift when you move between floors, which matters more than it sounds. If you have only hard floors, the self-clearing brush is wasted, and a cheaper series is the better choice.
products.bestFor: Carpeted homes with pets and stairs that want every convenience in one machine.

products.name: Kenmore Elite 21814 CrossOver bagged HEPA canister with Pet PowerMate
products.description:
The Elite 21814 is the older top-of-line machine, and its trick is the exclusive CrossOver floor nozzle, which switches quickly from hardwood to carpet. Combined with a Pet PowerMate motorized attachment for hair, dander and dirt, it handles mixed floors with fewer tool swaps.

A two-motor system powers the nozzles, and the listing describes a lightweight bagged HEPA design with an extended wand. It is an earlier generation than the 600 series, so it lacks the Hair Eliminator brushroll and the stair grip, but the CrossOver nozzle is a genuinely useful idea.

Clear hair from the powered attachment and keep the bag fresh. Because it is an older model, check that bags and filters are still stocked before buying. It suits a mixed-floor home that values smooth switching. The CrossOver idea is to avoid the tool swap that many owners skip, with the result that hard floors get a brush they do not need. A model that makes the right choice easy is a model that gets used properly.
products.bestFor: Mixed-floor homes that want one nozzle for hardwood and carpet.
pros: CrossOver nozzle for hardwood to carpet

products.name: Kenmore Elite Ultra Plush 700 Series bagged canister, 2 motors, HEPA

specList.label: Push-pull
specList.value: Up to 32 percent easier, per listing

products.description:
The Elite Ultra Plush 700 is the machine for thick carpet. Its Ultra Plush nozzle has vent inlets that the listing says make push-pull up to 32 percent easier on thick carpeting, which addresses the commonest complaint about powered heads: they grab and drag on deep pile.

Two motors deliver suction across carpets, rugs, stairs, upholstery and hard floors, and a completely sealed HEPA system is listed as trapping 99.97 percent of dust and particles down to 0.3 microns. It sits at the top of the range in features, with the sealing and the plush head the main upgrades.

Clear the nozzle of hair and change the bag before it is full. The easier push-pull claim is the maker's comparison, so judge it by feel when you try it. It suits a home with plush carpet and allergies. Thick carpet is the hardest surface for a powered head, because the pile pulls the nozzle down and the brush drags. A vented nozzle reduces that suction on the pile, and a lighter push means you vacuum longer without tiring.
products.bestFor: Homes with thick plush carpet and a need for sealed HEPA.
pros: Ultra Plush nozzle eases push-pull on thick carpet
cons: Push-pull claim is a maker comparison

products.name: Kenmore 500 Series bagless canister with Hair Eliminator brushroll, HEPA
products.description:
The 500 series is the bagless rung of the ladder. Cyclonic technology and two motors drive a carpet nozzle with a Hair Eliminator brushroll, and a HEPA filter is listed as trapping 99.97 percent of dust down to 0.3 microns, so the specification mirrors the bagged models.

The cyclonic cup lets you see what you have collected and avoids the cost of bags. The compromise is emptying, which releases dust at the bin, and filters that load faster than a bag does. It suits a household that vacuums carpets, hard floors and stairs and dislikes buying bags.

Empty the cup over a bag or outdoors, and wash the filters on schedule. Let them dry fully before refitting. Households that prefer a bin to a bag should start with this one. A clear cup lets you spot a lost earring or a coin before it clogs the hose, which a bag would hide. If anyone in the house has allergies, empty the cup outdoors and wear a simple dust mask.
products.bestFor: Households that want the Kenmore feature set without buying bags.

products.name: Kenmore 81414 400 Series bagged canister, sealed air path, 9.5 ft wand
products.description:
The 81414 is the 400 series with an extended telescoping wand. A completely sealed air path with HEPA filtration is listed as trapping 99.97 percent of dust and debris down to 0.3 microns, which is the feature that defines the series.

Two motors give strong suction on carpets, rugs, stairs, upholstery and hard floors, and the wand extends to 9.5 ft with a detachable handle for above-floor work. It has no motorized pet nozzle on the listing, so it leans on suction and a plain floor tool. For a sealed path with the longest reach in the range, it is the choice.

Check the bag and lid seating on every change and replace worn gaskets. Pull the bag by its collar when it is three quarters full so the self-sealing flap shuts. A telescoping wand is a joy for cobwebs and curtain tops, and a detachable handle makes the hose easier to hold for upholstery. If you often clean stairs, add the 600 series grip to your wish list, because the 81414 has no equivalent.
products.bestFor: Homes that want a sealed air path and the longest reach in the range.
cons: No motorized nozzle on the listing
Seal depends on a seated bag

products.name: Kenmore 81214 200 Series bagged canister, 2 motors, HEPA, 3 tools
products.description:
The 81214 is the entry rung of the ladder. Four height adjustments tune airflow to different surfaces, and an enhanced HEPA filter system is listed as trapping 99.97 percent of debris, capturing dander and dust inside the vacuum.

Three cleaning tools ship with it, and the listing says it suits the whole home, den, kitchen, car or garage. It has no Pet PowerMate, no extended wand and no sealed-path claim beyond the HEPA system, so it is the plainest of the range. That plainness keeps the weight down and the price low.

Check the height setting when you change floors and change the bag before it is full. For a first canister with HEPA, it is the sensible start. It also makes sense as a second machine for a basement or a rental, where you do not want to risk a pricier vacuum. Because it shares bags and filters with other 200 series models, replacements are easy to find.
products.bestFor: First-time canister buyers who want HEPA at the lowest tier of the range.
pros: Two motors and HEPA at an entry tier

buyingCriteria.explanation: The 200 series is the entry HEPA machine, the 400 adds a sealed air path and reach, the 500 is bagless, the 600 adds the Pet PowerMate and Pop-N-Go and the Elite 700 adds the Ultra Plush head. Choose the rung that adds the one thing you need. Paying for the whole ladder is wasteful. A short list of questions helps: do you have pets, thick carpet or allergies, and do you climb stairs? Each yes points to a specific series, and a household with no yes can safely start at the bottom.

The Hair Eliminator brushroll on the 600 and 500 series removes hair from the roller as it spins. On carpeted pet homes it saves a weekly chore. Older models without it need scissors. Even a self-clearing brush benefits from a glance every few weeks, because hair can bunch at the bearings and the roller ends. Cut it away with a pair of small scissors, and the head will run quieter and last longer.

The 400 series and the Elite 700 list a completely sealed air path with HEPA at 99.97 percent down to 0.3 microns. A sealed path keeps fine dust inside. For allergies it is worth paying for. Remember that the seal depends on the bag collar and lid seating, so keep the gaskets clean and replace them when they flatten. A listing that names the sealed path is a better sign than one that only names a filter.

The Elite 700's Ultra Plush nozzle eases push-pull on thick pile, the Elite 21814's CrossOver switches from hardwood to carpet, and the 600's Pop-N-Go avoids bending. Match the head to the floor you clean most. If you have wall-to-wall plush, the Ultra Plush head is worth the premium. If you have a few rugs on boards, the Pop-N-Go on the 600 is enough, and a plain head on the 200 series will do.

Most of the range is bagged, which contains dust, while the 500 is bagless and saves bag costs. A bagged HEPA machine is the better health choice. A bagless one is cheaper to run. Over five years the bag cost is modest, and the clean emptying is the bigger benefit for anyone sensitive to dust. If you choose the 500, wash the filters monthly and keep them dry before refitting.

The 400 and 600 series extend to 9.5 ft, and a two-motor body is heavier than a one-motor machine. For stairs, reach and a stair grip help. For a single level, weight matters less. Before you buy, lift the body by its handle and hold it for a few seconds, because a two-motor machine can feel heavy after a day of cleaning. If you struggle, the 200 series or a single-motor machine from another range may suit you better.

specDecoder.meaning: One motor for suction and a second for a motorized nozzle brush. It adds weight but lets the machine agitate carpet.
A brushroll that removes hair from the roller as it spins.
A body that routes all air through the filter with no leaks.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 400 series and Elite 700 list it.

specDecoder.meaning: The rated efficiency of the filter medium.
specDecoder.watchFor: It needs a sealed body to help.

specDecoder.meaning: A nozzle that switches between carpet and bare floor without a tool change.

howWeEvaluated.title: Series features
howWeEvaluated.description: We mapped what each series adds and judged how much each rung is worth. The 600 and Elite 700 led on features. The 200 led on simplicity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sealing and filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for sealed paths and HEPA. The 400 series and Elite 700 led.

howWeEvaluated.title: Carpet and floor heads
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared Hair Eliminator, Pet PowerMate, CrossOver and Ultra Plush heads. The Elite 700 led on thick pile and the 600 on pets.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked wand reach, grips and weight. The 600 and 400 series led on reach, and the 200 on weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read owner feedback patterns on bag fit, nozzle wear and parts supply. Series features drove the ranking, with relative cost as a minor factor.

cards.label: Bagged
cards.text: Most of the range contains dust in a bag and keeps suction steady. It needs bags.

cards.label: Bagless
cards.text: The 500 series avoids bag costs and shows the dirt. It releases dust at the bin and needs filter washing.

howToChoose.note: Pick bagged for allergies, and the 500 series if you dislike buying bags.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a self-clearing brush, a Pet PowerMate and a sealed air path for dander.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 600 Hair Eliminator pairs the brush with the powered nozzle, and the 400 and Elite 700 add the sealed path.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the Elite 700 or 600 if you have thick carpet, pets or allergies. The head and sealing earn the premium.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the 81214 if floors are mostly bare and small. The entry model does the basics.

maintenance.why: A full bag chokes the second motor and breaks the seal. Check the seat each time.
Hair collects at the roller ends. Cutting it away restores pickup.
A clogged filter cuts airflow. Dry washed filters fully.
A loose collar lets the telescoping wand slide down. Tighten or replace it.
A whipping plug damages walls and the body. Guide it back by hand.

faq.q: What do the Kenmore series numbers mean?
faq.a: They mark steps up the range. 200 is entry HEPA, 400 adds a sealed path and reach, 500 is bagless, 600 adds powered pet tools and Elite 700 adds the plush head.

faq.q: Which Kenmore is best for pets?
faq.a: The 600 Series with the Hair Eliminator brushroll, because the brush clears itself and the Pet PowerMate lifts embedded fur.

faq.q: Do all Kenmore canisters have HEPA?
faq.a: The listings for these six describe HEPA filtration. A sealed path is listed on the 400 series and Elite 700.

faq.q: Are the older Elite models worth buying?
faq.a: They can be good if parts are available. Check that bags and filters are still stocked before you buy.
Bagged contains dust better and suits allergies. Bagless saves bag costs but releases dust at the bin.
Many last a decade with care. Hoses, bags and nozzle brushes are the usual wear items.
